title: A randomized controlled study of daily aspirin to reduce liver stiffness and noninvasive fibrosis markers in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)
content:
by Khanisorn Meesri, Akarawich Boondamnoen, Kittithat Tantitanawat, Anuchit Suksamai, Sakkarin Chirapongsathorn

Objective

To evaluate the effect of low-dose aspirin on liver stiffness and noninvasive fibrosis markers in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in a randomized controlled study.

Methods

Participants with MASLD were randomly assigned to receive either aspirin or a placebo. The primary outcome was the change in liver stiffness at 6 months measured using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE). Secondary outcomes included changes in liver enzyme levels and noninvasive fibrosis scores (FIB-4, APRI, and NAFLD fibrosis score).

Results

At the 6-month follow-up, the aspirin group showed a statistically significant reduction in liver stiffness compared to placebo [−0.64 kPa (95% CI, −0.88 to −0.41) vs. −0.24 kPa (95% CI, −0.47 to 0.006), p = 0.019]. ALT levels also declined significantly in the aspirin group [−6.52 IU/L (95% CI, −11.20 to −1.85) vs. 0.70 IU/L (95% CI, −3.91 to 5.30), p = 0.032]. Significant reductions were observed in FIB-4 score [−0.09 (95% CI, −0.14 to −0.04) vs. 0.04 (95% CI, −0.01 to 0.09), p < 0.001] and APRI index [−0.05 (95% CI, −0.08 to −0.03) vs. 0.01 (95% CI, −0.01 to 0.03), p < 0.001]. In subgroup analyses among participants with baseline fibrosis stage greater than stage 2, fibrosis regression was numerically higher with aspirin but did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusion

Low-dose aspirin was associated with small, short-term reductions in noninvasive measures of liver stiffness in patients with MASLD. These changes may reflect reduced hepatic inflammation rather than structural fibrosis regression and require confirmation in larger, longer-term studies.

Trial registration

This trial was registered in the Thai Clinical Trials Registry on 4 July 2023 (Number: TCTR20230705001).
